title: Ledger record: dispatch acknowledgement
description: The actor's answer to a `dispatch_preflight` (issue #67, task t14): the second, separate action that commits a gated dispatch. It is the actor's own claim to have been told the operating facts and to have understood them -- a completion-claim-shaped statement, never evidence that it understood -- so it carries `proposed` authority and nothing else, and the ledger append layer refuses a derived one under any origin (RuleAcknowledgementNeverDerived): an engine that could derive an acknowledgement could clear its own gate. It names the preflight it answers BY DIGEST as well as by id, so `the actor acknowledged this briefing` cannot later be true of a different briefing.

verdict.description: The edit that turns the preflight's `hold` into a commitment, keeping the confirmation-file protocol's vocabulary. Only `proceed` is admitted today: an actor that cannot proceed has no verdict to record here, it simply does not acknowledge and the dispatch is refused when the window closes.

preflight_ref.description: The id of the `dispatch_preflight` record being acknowledged.

preflight_digest.description: The content digest of that preflight record. The id alone would say WHICH briefing was acknowledged; the digest says WHAT it said, which is the half that has to survive for the record to be worth anything.

acknowledged_by.description: The actor identity the acknowledgement is recorded for. Distinct from the envelope's `origin.actor_id`, which is the producer that wrote the record -- an operator may acknowledge on a bridge's behalf, and the two identities must stay separable when they do.

note.description: Free text from the acknowledging party. Documentary: a note is not a second verdict.
